draft.title: Maintenance
card: Maintenance is the part of the human resource process that keeps good staff once they have been hired and trained. Its aim is to keep them working well and wanting to stay.
Pay and conditions
Fair wages or salary, plus extras such as leave, flexible hours and bonuses. These show staff that their work is valued.
Safe workplace
Businesses must provide a safe place to work under work health and safety laws. This protects staff from injury and illness.
Support
Help for staff with workplace or personal problems, such as counselling, mentoring and ways to raise concerns. Staff who feel supported are more likely to stay.
draft.remember: Maintenance keeps good staff by treating them well, through pay, conditions, safety and support.

a.q: Which action is an example of maintenance in the human resource process?
opts: Offering flexible hours so staff can balance family life
Placing job advertisements to fill a vacant position
Running an induction day for newly hired workers
Paying a worker out when their role is no longer needed
a.why: Flexible hours are a condition of work that helps keep current staff. Running an induction day is development, not maintenance, though it is the most tempting option because it also helps new staff settle in.
a.clue: Which action is aimed at keeping staff the business already has?

b.q: A bakery in Orange loses several bakers each year. Its owner, Priya, wants them to stay. Which step best fits maintenance?
opts: Adding a mentoring scheme and a way to raise concerns
Writing a new job description for baker vacancies
Interviewing applicants to replace the bakers who left
Training the bakers to use a new type of oven
b.why: A mentoring scheme and a way to raise concerns give staff support, which helps keep them. Training on a new oven builds skills, so it is development, and it does not directly address why staff are leaving.
b.clue: Which step is about supporting the staff who are still there, not hiring or skills?

b.best: Adding a mentoring scheme and a way to raise concerns
